_meta.note: Research only. NOT yet merged into stateLaws in index.html. index.html already carries CA TX FL NY IL PA OH GA NC MI, which are NOT in this file — together that is all 50 states plus DC.

conventions.sol_credit_card: Where authority is split, the number is the period a court is MOST LIKELY TO APPLY, not the most consumer-favorable one. Asserting a time-bar too early is the dangerous error in a mailed letter. Both positions are in the confidence note, and sol_contested is true.
conventions.fcra_equivalent: null unless the state has a SUBSTANTIVE analog — reinvestigation duty, accuracy standard, civil liability. Security-freeze statutes alone do not qualify.
conventions.garnishment_exempt: Formulas rather than dollar amounts wherever indexed to a state minimum wage, because hardcoded figures go stale.

_meta.extinguishes_note: NCLC counts three: Mississippi, Wisconsin and North Carolina (the last for debt-buyer-owned debts only, N.C. Gen. Stat. 58-70-115(4)). NC is already in index.html and its entry there has not been updated with this.
_meta.medical_debt_note: These differ in WHO they bind, which decides who the letter goes to. Oregon binds CRAs AND furnishers. VT, RI, WA, MN, MD, ME bind CRAs. Virginia binds ONLY providers and collection entities, not CRAs — a letter to a bureau citing Virginia law is aimed at the wrong party. New Jersey additionally VOIDS medical debt reported in violation (N.J.S.A. 56:11-62). Colorado's SUNSETS 2028-07-01. Nevada's SB 248 is a 60-day notice-and-wait window, NOT a ban.
_meta.preemption_caveat: Cornerstone Credit Union League v. CFPB, 2025 WL 1920148 (E.D. Tex. 2025-07-11) vacated the federal Medical Debt Rule and included dicta suggesting FCRA preempts state medical-debt reporting bans. Per NCLC that is non-binding — preemption was not litigated and no state statute was invalidated. All the laws above remain operative, but expect it to be raised. Maine's law has separately been litigated: CDIA v. Frey, 26 F.4th 1 (1st Cir. 2022), and on remand D. Me. held FCRA partially preempts its veterans'-debt timing provisions.
verify_before_use: WV sol_written / sol_credit_card — W. Va. Code 55-2-6 not fetched verbatim; published summaries disagree
RI garnishment — R.I. Gen. Laws 9-26-4 subsection numbering unverified
UT SOL — le.utah.gov served a navigation shell; rests on section captions, not the operative sentence
AK garnishment dollar figure — 8 AAC 95.030 is CPI-adjusted, no 2026 refresh confirmed
HI HRS 480-13 remedy figures — not pulled directly
MN SOL subdivision number — 541.05 subd. 1(1) not fetched verbatim
NJ 56:11-38 — could not confirm whether it creates a consumer private right of action or only agency-enforced liability
corrections_to_common_sources: MD garnishment: the widely repeated $145/week figure and the four-county carve-out are OUTDATED — current 15-601.1 uses 30x the STATE minimum wage
NE garnishment: the '85% head of family' figure is stated backwards everywhere — 25-1558 caps garnishment AT 15% for head of family
WV garnishment: sources citing 30x federal minimum wage are WRONG — 46A-2-130 says fifty times
VA garnishment: 30x is OUTDATED — raised to 40x effective 2022
DC garnishment: the federal 30x rule no longer applies — D.C. Law 22-296 replaced it with 40x the D.C. minimum wage
OR garnishment: figures below $254/week (commonly $218) are OUTDATED
WA: the reinvestigation duty is RCW 19.182.090, NOT .080 — commonly miscited
CO: the CFDCPA was renumbered in 2017 from C.R.S. 12-14-101 to 5-16-101
WI: 893.12 is often miscited as a part-payment revival statute — it concerns advance payment of tort damages

AK.name: Alaska
AK.fdcpa_equivalent: Alaska Collection Agencies Act, AS 08.24.010–.380; UTPA AS 45.50.471
AK.fdcpa_note: UTPA reaches ORIGINAL CREDITORS with treble damages or $500 (AS 45.50.531), 2-year SOL. Real advantage over federal FDCPA.
AK.garnishment_exempt: Weekly net earnings exempt to a CPI-adjusted figure (~$473/wk per 8 AAC 95.030) — re-verify before printing
AK.confidence: HIGH on SOL — single 3-year period for any contract, no written/oral split, no card ambiguity. MEDIUM on the garnishment dollar figure.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.fdcpa_note: No Alabama fair-debt statute. ADTPA (Ala. Code 8-19-5) reaches original creditors but is a general UDAP with a demand-letter precondition — do not cite as a state FDCPA analog.
AL.garnishment_exempt: 75% of wages exempt; only 25% reachable (Ala. Code 6-10-7)
AL.confidence: MEDIUM-LOW on sol_credit_card. Revolving card = open account under 6-2-37(1) = 3 years, but collectors replead as account stated for 6. Assert 3, do not state as settled.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.fdcpa_equivalent: Arkansas FDCPA, Ark. Code Ann. §§ 17-24-501 to -512
AR.fdcpa_note: Tracks federal FDCPA and EXCLUDES original creditors (§ 17-24-502(5)(D)(i)). No advantage.
AR.garnishment_exempt: Federal 25%/30x cap; plus first $25/week absolutely exempt (Ark. Code Ann. 16-66-208)
AR.confidence: MEDIUM on sol_credit_card. Rests on In re Pettingill, 403 B.R. 624 (Bankr. E.D. Ark. 2009) — bankruptcy court, not appellate. Where no cardholder agreement is produced, argue 3 years under 16-56-105. Also: 16-56-111 is expressly tolled by partial payment or written acknowledgment.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.fdcpa_equivalent: A.R.S. §§ 32-1001–32-1057; Consumer Fraud Act A.R.S. § 44-1521 et seq.
AZ.fdcpa_note: A.R.S. 32-1051 has NO private right of action (criminal only). Cite the Consumer Fraud Act, which reaches original creditors and carries an implied private action.
AZ.garnishment_exempt: Only 10% of disposable earnings garnishable (A.R.S. 33-1131(B), Prop. 209, Dec 2022); bank exemption $5,000
AZ.confidence: HIGH, no ambiguity. A.R.S. 12-548(A)(2) names credit card debt expressly at 6 years, and (B) makes Arizona's period control over a shorter foreign one — defeats the Delaware choice-of-law argument in Arizona courts.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.fdcpa_equivalent: Colorado FDCPA, C.R.S. §§ 5-16-101 et seq. (recodified 2017 from 12-14-101 — do NOT use the old cite)
CO.fdcpa_note: No original-creditor reach, but § 5-16-111(2)(b) requires a debt buyer to attach documentary proof it owns THAT debt. Wright v. Portfolio Recovery Associates, 2026 CO 36 (May 2026) held a blank-schedule bill of sale insufficient and imposed § 5-16-113 liability. Powerful current hook.
CO.garnishment_exempt: 80% of disposable earnings exempt; only 20% or the excess over 40x minimum wage (C.R.S. 13-54-104(2))
CO.medical_debt_law: C.R.S. § 5-18-109(1)(f) (HB 23-1126), eff. 2023-08-07. SUNSETS 2028-07-01 — any template citing it must be date-gated.
CO.confidence: HIGH. sol_credit_card=6 settled per Portercare Adventist Health System v. Lego, 286 P.3d 525 (Colo. 2012). Do not concede 3 years.

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.fdcpa_note: YES — one of the strongest original-creditor statutes in the country. § 36a-646 binds creditors with no third-party limit; § 36a-648 gives actual damages plus up to $1,000 and fees. CAVEAT: only a ONE-YEAR limitations period, and a bona fide error defense.
CT.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25% of disposable earnings or excess over 40x the higher of federal or CT minimum wage (§ 52-361a(f)) — protects more than the federal 30x
CT.medical_debt_law: Conn. Pub. Act 24-6, codified at Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 19a-673b and 20-7i. Eff. 2024-07-01.
CT.confidence: HIGH, no card split. § 52-576 covers 'an action for an account, or on any simple or implied contract' — 6 years however the claim is pleaded.

DC.name: District of Columbia
DC.fdcpa_equivalent: D.C. Code § 28-3814, as expanded by the Protecting Consumers from Unjust Debt Collection Practices Amendment Act of 2022 (D.C. Law 24-154)
DC.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS. The 2022 Act (eff. 2023-01-01) defines debt collector to include a person 'engaging directly or indirectly in debt collection' and separately defines 'original creditor'. One carve-out: § 28-3814(m)(3) exempts original creditors from that subsection's documentation requirements only. STRONG private action § 28-3814(u): actual damages, costs and fees, punitive, plus statutory penalties of $500 to $4,000 per violation. With West Virginia, the most collector-adverse statute researched.
DC.garnishment_exempt: Wages at or below 40x the D.C. minimum wage per week are FULLY exempt; above that a creditor may reach 25% of the excess (§ 16-572); hardship motion at § 16-572.01. FLAG: any source applying the federal 30x-federal rule to D.C. is OUTDATED — replaced by D.C. Law 22-296 (2018). D.C.'s minimum wage is indexed and rises each July 1, so compute rather than quote.
DC.confidence: Fetched from code.dccouncil.gov. § 12-301(a)(7) gives 3 years for written, oral and card alike with no split — with South Carolina the shortest researched. GARNISHMENT: resolved a conflict — a Legal Aid summary described 'gradually increasing' tiers, but the statutory text and an independent source confirm a single flat rule of 25% of the excess over 40x the D.C. minimum wage. Not on NCLC's medical-debt list.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.fdcpa_note: No fair-debt statute. Only the Consumer Fraud Act, 6 Del. C. § 2513, plus the new Medical Debt Protection Act (6 Del. C. ch. 25J) for medical debt specifically.
DE.garnishment_exempt: 85% of wages exempt; only 15% reachable — better than the federal 25% (10 Del. C. 4913)
DE.medical_debt_law: 6 Del. C. § 2507J (SS1 for SB 156, Delaware Medical Debt Protection Act, 6 Del. C. ch. 25J). Eff. 2025-10-27. Reporting to a CRA is an 'extraordinary collection action' under § 2502J(4)b.
DE.confidence: HIGH. MATTERS BEYOND DELAWARE: many national card issuers are Delaware-chartered and their agreements select Delaware law, so a consumer in a borrowing-statute state (e.g. Kentucky, KRS 413.320) may import Delaware's 3 years. Raise as an argument, never as settled.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.fdcpa_equivalent: Haw. Rev. Stat. ch. 443B; violations are UDAP under HRS § 480-2 via § 443B-20
HI.fdcpa_note: Ch. 443B is third-party only, but § 443B-20 channels violations into § 480-2, which DOES reach original creditors, with § 480-13 treble damages or a $1,000 minimum plus fees.
HI.garnishment_exempt: Graduated: 5% of first $100/month, 10% of next $100, 20% above $200 (HRS 652-1); federal 25% cap also applies
HI.confidence: HIGH on SOL, no card split — § 657-1(1) covers 'any debt founded upon any contract, obligation, or liability' with no written/oral fork. MEDIUM on the § 480-13 remedy figures; verify before printing.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.fdcpa_equivalent: Iowa Consumer Credit Code, Iowa Code §§ 537.7101–537.7103
IA.fdcpa_note: YES — the biggest original-creditor advantage in this batch. § 537.7102(5) defines debt collector to include collecting 'for the person' — a creditor collecting its own debt is covered, with no officer/employee carve-out.
IA.garnishment_exempt: Annual per-creditor sliding caps (Iowa Code 642.21): $250 under $12k income, up to 10% of earnings at $50k+
IA.confidence: MEDIUM on sol_credit_card and CONDITIONAL. Gemini Capital Group v. New (Iowa Ct. App. 2011, unpublished) applied the 5-year § 614.1(4) where an unsigned cardholder agreement needed parol evidence. Assert 5 and demand the writing; a proven signed contract gives the creditor 10.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.fdcpa_equivalent: Idaho Collection Agency Act, Idaho Code § 26-2229A; Idaho Consumer Protection Act §§ 48-601 to 48-619
ID.fdcpa_note: § 26-2229A is licensee-only. The ICPA is what reaches original creditors, with a private action at § 48-608.
ID.garnishment_exempt: Mirrors the federal floor — lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (Idaho Code 11-207(1))
ID.confidence: LOW-MEDIUM on sol_credit_card and genuinely split by fact pattern. No Idaho appellate decision resolves credit cards. Assert 5 only where an authenticated cardholder agreement exists; argue 4 under § 5-217 wherever the writing is not produced — the stronger consumer position. Idaho Code § 5-238 permits revival by partial payment.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.fdcpa_equivalent: Indiana Deceptive Consumer Sales Act, Ind. Code § 24-5-0.5-3(b)(20)
IN.fdcpa_note: DCSA reaches suppliers incl. original creditors BUT § 24-5-0.5-4(a) withholds the private right of action for debt-collection acts — AG enforcement only. Route private claims to the federal FDCPA.
IN.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage; court may reduce to 10% for good cause (Ind. Code 24-4.5-5-105)
IN.confidence: HIGH — every route lands on 6 years. Smither v. Asset Acceptance, 919 N.E.2d 1153 (Ind. Ct. App. 2010) held a card account is an open account under 34-11-2-7(1). Do NOT cite Ind. Code § 34-11-2-11 (10 years) — that is for written contracts NOT for the payment of money.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.fdcpa_equivalent: Kansas Consumer Protection Act, K.S.A. §§ 50-623 to 50-643
KS.fdcpa_note: YES — K.S.A. 50-624 defines supplier to include anyone who 'enforces' consumer transactions, capturing original creditors, assignees and debt buyers. § 50-627 unconscionability is especially useful against collection conduct.
KS.fcra_equivalent: K.S.A. §§ 50-701 to 50-722 — a genuine substantive FCRA analog, not just a freeze law
KS.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25%, excess over 30x federal minimum wage, or the claim (K.S.A. 60-2310); one garnishment per 30 days
KS.confidence: MEDIUM on sol_credit_card but the consumer-favorable number is the DEFAULT — 60-512(1) covers contracts 'expressed or implied but not in writing'. No Kansas appellate decision on cards. Assert 3 and demand the writing.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.fdcpa_note: Inverted: KRS 367.220(1) confers standing only on one who 'purchases or leases goods or services', and Kentucky reads in privity (Skilcraft line) — works against ORIGINAL CREDITORS, generally not against debt buyers.
KY.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (KRS 427.010(2))
KY.confidence: LOWEST of the batch. NO KENTUCKY APPELLATE COURT has decided which period governs credit cards. The 5-year figure rests on Conway v. Portfolio Recovery Associates, 13 F. Supp. 3d 711 (E.D. Ky. 2014) — persuasive only. Collector will argue 10 under 413.160 (or 15 under 413.090 pre-July-2014). Two wrinkles: KRS 413.320 is a borrowing statute that can import Delaware's 3 years; single-merchant store cards may fall under UCC 4 years, KRS 355.2-725.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.fdcpa_equivalent: La. R.S. 9:3562; LUTPA La. R.S. 51:1401 et seq.
LA.fdcpa_note: Reaches original creditors — 9:3562 binds 'the creditor'. Narrow though: mainly third-party contacts, no statutory damages. Use LUTPA for a broader theory (treble after AG notice, fees).
LA.garnishment_exempt: 75% of disposable earnings exempt, never less than 30x federal minimum wage/week (La. R.S. 13:3881(A)(1)(a))
LA.confidence: HIGH. Card = 3 as open account under art. 3494, settled practice. Oral is ALSO 10 (art. 3499 has no oral/written split) — the 3-year periods attach to transaction type, not absence of a writing. Art. 1762(1) uses 'extinguished' language but effect is remedy-barring and a new promise can create an enforceable obligation — do NOT claim the debt is void.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.fdcpa_equivalent: M.G.L. c. 93 § 49, enforced through c. 93A; AG regs 940 CMR 7.00
MA.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS EXPLICITLY — § 49 names 'a creditor or an attorney for a creditor, or an assignee of a creditor'. Violation is automatically a c. 93A unfair practice, giving a § 9 claim with $25 statutory minimum, up to treble for willful, and MANDATORY attorney's fees. Send the 30-day 93A demand letter first — it is a prerequisite and it is what creates the multiple-damages exposure. One of the strongest states in the country.
MA.garnishment_exempt: Greater of 85% of GROSS wages or 50x the greater of federal or Massachusetts minimum wage (M.G.L. c. 246 § 28) — among the most protective in the country
MA.confidence: HIGH. 6 years for both written and oral (c. 260 § 2 makes no distinction), so no card split. c. 260 § 1 gives 20 years under seal; c. 106 § 2-725 gives 4 for sale of goods, occasionally argued for retail cards. NOT on NCLC's 15-state medical-debt list despite a CFPB letter supporting a bill.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.fdcpa_equivalent: Maryland Consumer Debt Collection Act, Md. Code Com. Law §§ 14-201 to 14-204
MD.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — § 14-201(b) defines collector as anyone collecting a consumer-transaction debt, no carve-out. Private action § 14-203 includes emotional distress damages with or without physical injury. Also a CPA unfair practice (§ 13-301(14)(iii)) unlocking § 13-408 fee-shifting. § 14-202(8) carries a scienter element — plead knowledge.
MD.garnishment_exempt: Greater of 75% of disposable wages or 30x the STATE minimum wage per week (Md. Code Com. Law § 15-601.1)
MD.medical_debt_law: Md. Code Com. Law § 14-1213 (2025 HB 1020); provider-side ban at Health-Gen. §§ 24-2501, 24-2502. Eff. 2025-10-01. No sunset.
MD.confidence: HIGH. CORRECTION: the widely repeated '$145 per week' garnishment figure and the Caroline/Kent/Queen Anne's/Worcester county carve-out are OUTDATED — current § 15-601.1 uses 30x the state minimum wage with no county exception. Do not print $145. Note § 5-102 gives 12 years for a specialty under seal, which debt buyers occasionally invoke. 2025 HB 268 adds a 3-year medical-debt-specific SOL and a bar on suits under $500 — codified section not independently verified.

ME.name: Maine
ME.fdcpa_note: Generally does not reach a creditor collecting in its own name, but DOES capture a creditor using another name. Private action § 11054: actual + up to $1,000 ($2,000 vs a debt buyer), costs, fees. STANDOUT: § 11013(8) bars a collection action more than 6 years after LAST ACTIVITY 'notwithstanding any other applicable statute of limitations', and once expired 'any subsequent payment toward, written or oral affirmation of or other activity on the debt does not revive or extend' it. Non-revival rule stronger than the general SOL — the single most useful Maine cite.
ME.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25% or excess over 40x federal (or higher state) minimum wage (9-A M.R.S. § 5-105)
ME.confidence: HIGH. CAVEAT: litigated — CDIA v. Frey, 26 F.4th 1 (1st Cir. 2022); on remand D. Me. (2024-01-11) held FCRA PARTIALLY preempts the veterans'-medical-debt timing provisions while the non-veteran reporting restriction survived. Expect preemption to be raised.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.fdcpa_equivalent: Minn. Stat. §§ 332.31-332.45 (prohibited practices § 332.37); Minn. Stat. ch. 332C (medical debt)
MN.fdcpa_note: Does NOT reach original creditors. FLAG: NO EXPRESS PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION under ch. 332 — enforcement is the Commerce Commissioner and the AG. Whether § 8.31 subd. 3a reaches ch. 332 is unsettled. Do not promise a consumer damages under ch. 332. By contrast ch. 332C DOES have one: § 332C.05(b) actual + up to $1,000 per violation + fees, trebled for willful under (c).
MN.garnishment_exempt: Graduated (Minn. Stat. § 571.922, revised 2024): 25% if weekly income exceeds 80x minimum wage; 15% if 60-80x; 10% if 40-60x; nothing below 40x
MN.medical_debt_law: Minn. Stat. ch. 332C (Debt Fairness Act, 2024 ch. 368). Eff. 2024-10-01. § 332C.03(a) bars collecting parties from reporting; (b) bars CRAs from including it. No sunset.
MN.confidence: HIGH on ch. 332/332C. fcra_equivalent NULL BY DESIGN — ch. 13C is access-and-freeze only (annual free report, freezes, employer disclosure, adverse action); no reinvestigation duty, no accuracy standard, no willful/negligent liability. LOWER confidence on the SOL subdivision number — verify § 541.05 subd. 1(1) before printing.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.fdcpa_note: No dedicated analog. Courts apply the MMPA, Mo. Rev. Stat. § 407.020, private action § 407.025 (actual, punitive, fees, class actions allowed). Not limited to third-party collectors, so it reaches original creditors — but you must tie conduct to a covered transaction, an extra element the FDCPA does not require. Tightened by 2020 amendments (reliance and ascertainable-loss pleading).
MO.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25%, excess over 30x federal minimum wage, or 10% if head of family and a Missouri resident (Mo. Rev. Stat. § 525.030(2))
MO.confidence: SPLIT IS REAL. Consumer position 5 years under § 516.120: Capital One Bank v. Creed, No. 27752 (Mo. Ct. App. S.D. 2007) held that where no signed written promise was produced the 5-year statute applies. Counter: § 516.110(1) reaches 'any writing for the payment of money' — 10 years — and debt buyers press it. Missouri's test is whether the promise AND an ascertainable amount appear from the writing itself; revolving balances generally do not. Assert 5 only where no signed agreement is produced. No Supreme Court resolution found.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.fdcpa_note: NO state FDCPA analog and no collection-agency licensing. MCPA § 75-24-15 private action is unusually weak — must exhaust the AG's informal dispute program, limited recovery, no private class actions. Consumers rely on the federal FDCPA.
MS.garnishment_exempt: ALL wages fully exempt for the first 30 days after service (Miss. Code § 85-3-4(1)); thereafter lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage
MS.confidence: VERIFIED EXTINGUISHMENT. § 15-1-3(1) verbatim: 'The completion of the period of limitation prescribed to bar any action, shall defeat and extinguish the right as well as the remedy.' Critically § 15-1-3(2) permits revival by part payment or acknowledgment ONLY 'the statute of limitations not having run' — so after 3 years a later payment CANNOT revive. Extinguishment plus no post-expiration revival is the strongest time-barred position of any state researched; quote it verbatim.

MT.name: Montana
MT.fdcpa_note: NO analog for consumer collections. Title 17 ch. 4 is about the STATE collecting debts owed to it — do NOT cite it in a consumer letter. Fallback is the MCPA, § 30-14-103 with private action § 30-14-133 (actual or $500 whichever greater, court may treble, fees). Not limited to third-party collectors so it can reach an original creditor, but every claim is a general unfairness theory.
MT.fcra_equivalent: Mont. Code Ann. Title 31 ch. 3 pt. 1, §§ 31-3-101 to 31-3-153 (compliance § 31-3-114; disputed accuracy § 31-3-124; willful § 31-3-142; negligent § 31-3-143)
MT.garnishment_exempt: Federal CCPA limits — lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (Mont. Code Ann. § 25-13-614)
MT.confidence: § 27-2-202 verbatim: (1) 8 years on an instrument in writing; (2) 5 years on 'a contract, account, or promise not founded on an instrument in writing'. Card = 5 because (2) expressly names 'account'. Counter: 8 years where a signed agreement is produced. No Montana Supreme Court decision found either way — 8 is a live risk, flag it.

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.fdcpa_note: Does NOT reach original creditors — § 13-05-02.3(9) expressly exempts 'creditors collecting their own debts'. FLAG: NO PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION; enforced administratively by the Department of Financial Institutions (up to $5,000 per violation) and criminally (class C felony). A consumer gets nothing directly from it. Fallback for private damages is N.D.C.C. ch. 51-15, private action § 51-15-09 (actual, treble, fees).
ND.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25% or excess over 40x federal minimum wage, REDUCED by $20 for each dependent family member residing with the debtor (N.D.C.C. § 32-09.1-03); debtor must give the employer a signed dependent list within 10 days
ND.confidence: HIGH. § 28-01-16(1) covers 'a contract, obligation, or liability, express or implied' — single 6-year period, no card split. § 28-01-15 gives 10 years on a judgment or sealed instrument. fcra null by design — ch. 51-33 is a freeze statute only.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.fdcpa_note: No general analog. Collection Agency Act §§ 45-601 et seq. is licensing only — NO PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION. Fallback is the Consumer Protection Act § 59-1602/§ 59-1609 (actual, court may treble, fees) but § 59-1617 exempts conduct regulated by other regulatory bodies, which collectors invoke. Nothing gives Nebraska consumers an edge over the federal FDCPA against original creditors.
NE.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 25%, or 15% if head of a family, or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 25-1558)
NE.confidence: DELIBERATELY NOT the consumer-favorable default. The 4-year open-account theory under § 25-206 is arguable but Nebraska practitioners uniformly treat card agreements as written contracts under § 25-205 at 5 years, and no Nebraska appellate decision applies 4 to a credit card. Set to 5 because a wrong SOL in a mailed letter is worse than a conservative one; raise 4 as an argument. CORRECTION: the commonly cited '85% head of family' is wrong — § 25-1558 caps garnishment AT 15% for head of family (85% protected). fcra null — §§ 8-2601 to 8-2615 is freeze only.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.fdcpa_equivalent: NH Unfair, Deceptive or Unreasonable Collection Practices Act, RSA ch. 358-C
NH.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — RSA 358-C:1 VIII(a) defines debt collector as anyone who 'enforces or attempts to enforce an obligation' from a consumer credit transaction, with no carve-out; (b) and (c) then add fee-based collectors and debt buyers. Private action RSA 358-C:4 I: the GREATER of $200 plus costs and fees per violation, or all damages proximately caused. May be raised as a counterclaim in the collector's own suit. Short 3-year SOL plus a creditor-reaching statute makes NH one of the better states.
NH.fcra_equivalent: RSA ch. 359-B (accuracy 359-B:7 II; reinvestigation 359-B:11; willful 359-B:16; negligent 359-B:17)
NH.garnishment_exempt: NH effectively bars wage garnishment for ordinary consumer debts — RSA 512:21 II exempts pre-writ wages except on a NH-court judgment; where one exists, 50x federal minimum wage per week is protected
NH.confidence: HIGH. RSA 508:4 I is a single 3-year period for 'all personal actions', no written/oral split, no card split. CAVEAT: RSA 358-C:2 contains an applicability/exemption provision and some financial institutions argue partial exemption — confirm before asserting coverage against a bank specifically.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.fdcpa_note: No dedicated analog. Fallback is the CFA, N.J.S.A. 56:8-1 et seq., private action § 56:8-19 with MANDATORY TREBLE damages plus fees on proof of ascertainable loss — powerful, and not limited to third-party collectors. Limitation is doctrinal: NJ courts are inconsistent about whether post-contract collection activity is 'in connection with the sale or advertisement of merchandise', so CFA coverage of pure collection conduct is contested and fact-dependent.
NJ.garnishment_exempt: Ordinarily no more than 10% of wages; more only if income exceeds 250% of the federal poverty level (N.J.S.A. 2A:17-56). For MEDICAL debt, N.J.S.A. 56:11-60 bars garnishment of patients under 600% of poverty, eff. 2025-07-22
NJ.medical_debt_law: Louisa Carman Medical Debt Relief Act, P.L. 2024 c. 48, N.J.S.A. 56:11-56 to 56:11-63. Reporting ban § 56:11-58 and VOIDING provision § 56:11-62(a) took effect 2024-07-22; interest cap, garnishment ban, notice and waiting-period provisions 2025-07-22. No sunset.
NJ.confidence: HIGH. NOTE § 56:11-62 — medical debt reported in violation is VOID, not merely unreportable. Unusual and strong; the most valuable NJ cite for a dispute letter. LOWER confidence on whether § 56:11-38 creates a consumer private right of action or only agency-enforced liability — verify before promising damages under the state FCRA.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.fdcpa_equivalent: New Mexico Unfair Practices Act, NMSA 1978 §§ 57-12-1 to 57-12-26
NM.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — § 57-12-2(D) expressly covers misrepresentation 'in the extension of credit or in the collection of debts by a person in the regular course of the person's trade or commerce'. Debt collection and credit extension are named in the statute itself. Private action § 57-12-10: actual or $100 whichever greater, up to treble for willful, plus fees. The Collection Agency Regulatory Act is licensing-only with no private remedy.
NM.fcra_equivalent: NMSA 1978 §§ 56-3-1 to 56-3-8 — LIMITED, not a full analog (obsolescence § 56-3-6; civil liability § 56-3-7)
NM.garnishment_exempt: Greater of 75% of disposable earnings or 40x the highest applicable minimum wage where earned (NMSA 1978 § 35-12-7); exempt amounts stay exempt in a bank account if traceable
NM.confidence: SPLIT IS REAL. 4 years under § 37-1-4 ('accounts and unwritten contracts') is the consumer position; counter is 6 under § 37-1-3(A) with a signed agreement. No controlling appellate decision found. ALSO CHECK § 37-1-5 (4 years for causes arising outside NM) — many card agreements select Delaware, South Dakota or Utah law, and NM's borrowing rule can independently cap at 4 years; often the better argument. fcra_equivalent QUALIFIED — could not confirm any reinvestigation duty; do not represent it as equivalent to FCRA § 1681i.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.fdcpa_note: Does NOT reach original creditors — ch. 649 is collection-agency licensing and NRS 649.020 excludes creditors collecting their own debts. FLAG: no clear private right of action under ch. 649; enforcement is the Commissioner of Financial Institutions. The workaround is NRS 598.0923 coupled with the private action at NRS 41.600 (actual damages, equitable relief, fees). To reach an ORIGINAL creditor in Nevada use NRS 41.600, not ch. 649.
NV.fcra_equivalent: Nev. Rev. Stat. ch. 598C (reinvestigation NRS 598C.160; willful NRS 598C.190; negligent NRS 598C.200)
NV.garnishment_exempt: 82% of disposable earnings exempt if gross weekly wage was $770 or less, else 75%; or 50x federal minimum wage, whichever is greater (NRS 21.090(1)(g))
NV.medical_debt_law: NRS 649.366-649.369 (SB 248, 2021). Eff. 2021-07-01. NOTICE-AND-WAIT ONLY, not a ban: 60-day written notice before collecting medical debt, and no reporting during that window. After 60 days reporting is not prohibited.
NV.confidence: HIGH on SOL/credit reporting/garnishment. Card = 4 under 11.190(2)(a)/(2)(c) is standard; counter is 6 under (1)(b) with a signed agreement. Nevada is NOT on NCLC's 15-state list and SB 248 must not be described as a reporting ban.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.fdcpa_note: NO comprehensive state collection statute. OCPA 15 O.S. § 751 et seq. is a general UDAP with a private action at § 761.1 but does not regulate collection conduct and is not treated as an FDCPA analog. Consumers rely on the federal FDCPA.
OK.garnishment_exempt: 75% exempt; lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (12 O.S. § 1171.1; 31 O.S. § 1(A)(18)); undue-hardship exemption on application
OK.confidence: CONTESTED. 5 is what courts most commonly apply. Consumer position is 3 under § 95(A)(2) — an unsigned issuer-drafted agreement is not a 'contract, agreement, or promise in writing'. Counter: acceptance by use makes it written. No controlling appellate decision found.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.fdcpa_equivalent: Oregon Unlawful Debt Collection Practices Act, ORS 646.639-646.643
OR.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — ORS 646.639 defines debt collector as a person who 'collects or attempts to collect a debt owed, or alleged to be owed, to a creditor or debt buyer'. Oregon did NOT import the federal creditor exemption. Private action ORS 646.641: actual or $200 minimum, punitive, fees.
OR.garnishment_exempt: Greater of 75% or $254/week ($509/two weeks, $545/half-month, $1,090/month) exempt (ORS 18.385). FLAG: figures below $254/week (commonly $218) are OUTDATED — raised effective 2020. Fixed by statute, not indexed.
OR.medical_debt_law: ORS 646A.677(11)-(12), SB 605 (2025). Eff. 2026-01-01. FULL BAN binding BOTH sides — CRAs may not include medical debt, and no person may report it. Court may declare medical debt void as a remedy. No sunset.
OR.confidence: HIGH. Broadest of the medical-debt bans because it binds furnishers as well as CRAs — a letter can go to either. fcra null: ORS 646A.600-628 is identity-theft/freeze; the new § 646A.677(11) imposes one CRA duty but only as to medical debt.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.fdcpa_equivalent: Rhode Island FDCPA, R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 19-14.9
RI.fdcpa_note: Does NOT reach original creditors collecting in their own name — § 19-14.9-3 mirrors the federal definition and sweeps in a creditor only when using another name. HAS a private action: § 19-14.9-13, actual plus up to $1,000 additional, costs and fees; class recovery capped at $500,000. One-year limitations period on the claim.
RI.garnishment_exempt: Scattered rather than consolidated — § 9-26-4 exempts specified wages including a small flat exemption and wages of public-assistance recipients for one year; federal CCPA cap applies as a floor. LOW CONFIDENCE — verify subsection numbering before use.
RI.medical_debt_law: R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-60 §§ 6-60-1 to 6-60-5. Eff. 2025-07-01. FULL BAN, no notice window, no sunset. § 6-60-3 verbatim: 'No credit reporting agency shall acquire, record, or report any medical debt, in any manner.'
RI.confidence: § 9-1-13(a) is a 10-year catch-all for 'all civil actions' with no shorter contract provision, so all three are 10 — the longest in the set. A 4-year UCC argument (§ 6A-2-725) governs buyer-seller sales contracts and is not generally applied to a card issuer's claim. GARNISHMENT IS THE WEAKEST ITEM — do not put a dollar amount in a letter without checking § 9-26-4.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.fdcpa_equivalent: S.C. Consumer Protection Code, Title 37, esp. § 37-5-108
SC.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — § 37-5-108 targets the conduct of 'the creditor' and assignees, not just third parties. Provides actual damages and, on a finding of unconscionable collection conduct, statutory relief plus fees. No separate collection-agency licensing act. Coverage depends on the debt qualifying as a 'consumer credit transaction' under § 37-1-301.
SC.garnishment_exempt: South Carolina effectively PROHIBITS wage garnishment for ordinary consumer and commercial debt — available only for support, taxes and federally guaranteed student loans (§ 37-5-104). The most consumer-favorable garnishment posture researched. Bank levies still possible.
SC.confidence: § 15-3-530(1) verbatim: 'an action upon a contract, obligation, or liability, express or implied' — 3 years, no written/oral distinction, among the shortest in the country, no card split. MODERATE confidence on the § 37-5-104 section number and on § 37-5-108 reaching pure collection conduct — no case verified.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.fdcpa_note: NO state analog. SDCL ch. 37-29 is collection-agency licensing and bonding with NO private right of action. SDCL ch. 37-24 has a private action (§ 37-24-31) but is not a collection statute. Consumers rely on the federal FDCPA.
SD.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 20% of disposable earnings or excess over 40x federal minimum wage (SDCL 21-18-51) — the 20% cap beats the federal 25%; additional head-of-family reduction by dependents
SD.confidence: § 15-2-13(1) verbatim — 'express or implied' describes the nature of the obligation, NOT the form, so no written/oral split and no card split. MODERATE on garnishment specifics; dependent add-on figures vary between sources — verify before quoting a dollar amount.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.fdcpa_equivalent: Tennessee Collection Service Act, Tenn. Code Ann. § 62-20-101 et seq.
TN.fdcpa_note: NO PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION — the critical Tennessee flag. Licensing statute enforced by the Collection Service Board; no consumer damages remedy and courts have generally declined to imply one. Does NOT reach original creditors (§ 62-20-103 exempts persons collecting their own accounts). Practical route is the TCPA § 47-18-109, though narrowed by 2011 amendments and its application to collection conduct is contested.
TN.garnishment_exempt: 75% exempt; lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (§§ 26-2-106, 26-2-107), plus a $2.50/week per dependent child under 16 exemption that has not been raised in decades
TN.confidence: § 28-3-109(a)(3) 'Actions on contracts not otherwise expressly provided for' — 6 years, no written/oral distinction. Searched specifically for a card split and found none genuine; the 4-year UCC argument governs sale-of-goods contracts, not a card issuer's claim. MODERATE on 'no private right of action' — structure confirmed, no case fetched. Do not assert a TCSA damages claim without checking current case law.

UT.name: Utah
UT.fdcpa_note: NO state analog. Utah Code § 12-1-1 et seq. is registration and bonding with no conduct code and no private right of action. UCSPA § 13-11-19 has a private action but regulates 'suppliers' in consumer sales and is generally unavailable against collection conduct. Some restrictions in the Consumer Credit Code § 70C-7-101 et seq. Nothing reaches original creditors as collectors.
UT.garnishment_exempt: 75% exempt; lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (§ 70C-7-103; procedure Utah R. Civ. P. 64D)
UT.confidence: le.utah.gov served a navigation shell on two attempts — the 6/4 split rests on official section CAPTIONS plus Justia's index, not a verbatim fetch of the operative sentence. Card reported as 6 on the standard reasoning that a written agreement is an instrument in writing; a consumer can argue 4 under § 78B-2-307 where the agreement is not produced, and no Utah appellate decision forecloses it.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.fdcpa_note: NO state analog. VCPA § 59.1-196 et seq. has a private action (§ 59.1-204: actual or $500, up to $1,000 willful, fees) but governs 'suppliers' in 'consumer transactions', and Virginia courts have generally held collecting a debt is not itself a consumer transaction — so the VCPA is usually NOT available against pure collection conduct. The separate Medical Debt Protection Act does create medical-debt duties enforceable under ch. 17.
VA.garnishment_exempt: 75% exempt; lesser of 25% or excess over 40x federal minimum wage (§ 34-29). FLAG: sources citing 30x for Virginia are OUTDATED — raised to 40x effective 2022. MODERATE — not fetched verbatim.
VA.medical_debt_law: Va. Code § 59.1-444.4, Medical Debt Protection Act (2024 Acts ch. 751). Eff. 2024-04-17. FULL BAN but runs against the FURNISHER side, not CRAs — bars facilities, licensed professionals and EMS agencies from reporting medical debt, and bars collection entities from reporting a collection or attempt. No sunset.
VA.confidence: SHARPEST SPLIT IN THE DATASET. 5 is what courts most often apply, but § 8.01-246(2) requires a contract 'in writing and signed by the party to be charged' — a typical cardholder agreement is issuer-drafted and never signed, pushing the claim into § 8.01-246(4)'s 3 years. Counter: the signed credit application, acceptance by use, or account stated. Turns on whether a signed writing is produced — raise the 3-year argument whenever it is not. SEPARATELY: § 8.01-246(B) sets a medical-debt-specific SOL of only 3 years from the final invoice due date. Virginia's ban does not bind CRAs, so aim the letter at the provider or collection entity.

VT.name: Vermont
VT.fdcpa_equivalent: Vermont Consumer Protection Rule CP 104, adopted under 9 V.S.A. § 2453; licensing 8 V.S.A. § 2201
VT.fdcpa_note: Vermont's collection code is a RULE, not a statute — cite CP 104 together with its enabling statute. A CP 104 violation is a CPA violation with a private action at 9 V.S.A. § 2461(b): actual or $200 minimum, exemplary up to treble, plus fees. CP 104 is generally understood to reach creditors collecting their own debts but the rule's definitional text was NOT verified — treat original-creditor coverage as probable, not confirmed.
VT.fcra_equivalent: Vermont FCRA, 9 V.S.A. §§ 2480a-2480g (disputed accuracy § 2480d; civil liability § 2480f)
VT.garnishment_exempt: For consumer debt, greater of 85% of disposable weekly earnings or 40x federal minimum wage (12 V.S.A. § 3170) — only 15% reachable; court may exempt more on hardship. MODERATE — percentages not fetched verbatim.
VT.medical_debt_law: 9 V.S.A. § 2466d (with 18 V.S.A. § 9485(b)). Eff. 2025-07-01. FULL BAN, no notice window, no sunset. Verbatim: 'A credit reporting agency shall not report or maintain in the file on a consumer information relating to a medical debt.' Covers medical, dental and mental health services; excludes veterinary, certain card charges, home equity debt.
VT.confidence: One of only TWO jurisdictions in this batch with a REAL substantive FCRA analog (Washington the other). § 2480f(b) fetched verbatim creating a private action for damages, injunctive relief, punitive for willful, costs and fees, with a willful floor of actual or $100. 12 V.S.A. § 511 gives 6 years, no written/oral split.

WA.name: Washington
WA.fdcpa_equivalent: Washington Collection Agency Act, RCW ch. 19.16 (RCW 19.16.250, 19.16.260)
WA.fdcpa_note: Does NOT reach original creditors — RCW 19.16.100 excludes 'any person whose collection activities are carried on in his, her, or its true name and are directly related to the operation of a business other than that of a collection agency'. HAS an effective private action by an unusual route: RCW 19.16.440 declares violations to be unfair practices for purposes of ch. 19.86, supplying the private action, treble damages to the statutory cap, and fees under RCW 19.86.090.
WA.fcra_equivalent: Washington FCRA, RCW ch. 19.182 (accuracy 19.182.060(2); reinvestigation 19.182.090; civil liability 19.182.150)
WA.garnishment_exempt: CONSUMER DEBT: greater of 80% of disposable weekly earnings or 35x the STATE minimum wage (RCW 6.27.150(4)). Non-consumer: 75% or 35x federal. Student loans: 85% or 50x state. FLAG: a flat 75%/35x-federal rule for consumer debt is OUTDATED, and any dollar figure goes stale annually because the state minimum wage is indexed each January 1 — compute, do not quote.
WA.medical_debt_law: RCW 19.182.040(1)(g), with 'medical debt' defined by RCW 19.16.100; related RCW 19.16.250(28), RCW 70.41.400(2). Eff. 2025-07-27. FULL BAN on inclusion in consumer reports, narrow exceptions for certain high-value credit and employment purposes. No sunset. Binds CRAs directly.
WA.confidence: Best-documented jurisdiction researched. Real substantive FCRA analog verified section by section. NOTE the reinvestigation duty is RCW 19.182.090, NOT .080 — commonly miscited. Willful liability: actual plus a $1,000 monetary penalty plus costs and fees; negligent: actual plus costs and fees.

WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.fdcpa_equivalent: Wisconsin Consumer Act, Wis. Stat. ch. 427 (§ 427.104)
WI.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — § 427.103 defines debt collection as collecting claims 'owed or due or alleged to be owed or due a merchant by a customer' and debt collector as 'any person engaging, directly or indirectly, in debt collection', with NO creditor exemption. Private action § 427.105 plus remedies and fees under §§ 425.304, 425.308.
WI.garnishment_exempt: 80% of disposable earnings exempt — only 20% reachable (§ 812.34). TOTAL exemption frequently overlooked: earnings wholly exempt if household income is below the federal poverty line, or the debtor receives need-based public assistance (or did within 6 months, or is eligible). If 20% would push the household below poverty, garnishment is limited to the excess.
WI.confidence: EXTINGUISHMENT VERIFIED. § 893.05 verbatim: 'When the period within which an action may be commenced on a Wisconsin cause of action has expired, the right is extinguished as well as the remedy.' REVIVAL: a post-expiration payment does NOT revive, for two independent reasons — § 893.45 requires a signed writing for any new promise, and once § 893.05 extinguishes the right there is nothing left to revive. § 893.12 is often miscited here; it concerns advance payment of tort damages, not part-payment revival. TRAP: the borrowing statute § 893.07 applies the shorter of Wisconsin's period and that of the state where the claim arose — many card agreements select Delaware or South Dakota, so check the choice-of-law clause before assuming 6.

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.fdcpa_equivalent: West Virginia Consumer Credit and Protection Act, W. Va. Code §§ 46A-2-122 to 46A-2-129a
WV.fdcpa_note: REACHES ORIGINAL CREDITORS — the clearest original-creditor coverage of any state researched. West Virginia deliberately did not adopt the federal creditor exemption; a creditor collecting its own debt, including a bank, is subject to the full WVCCPA. The only carve-out in § 46A-2-122 is for WV-licensed attorneys collecting in their own name. Private action § 46A-5-101. Post-2015 amendments: 4-year limitations period for claims filed on or after 2015-09-01, penalties capped near $1,000 per violation, class recovery capped at the greater of $175,000 or total outstanding indebtedness, and a cure safe harbor at § 46A-5-101(5).
WV.garnishment_exempt: Lesser of 20% of disposable weekly earnings or excess over 50x federal minimum wage (§ 46A-2-130) — verified verbatim. FLAG: sources citing 30x for West Virginia are WRONG; the statute says fifty times. With the 20% cap, among the more protective researched.
WV.confidence: An automated read of the bare statute initially concluded original creditors fall OUTSIDE the WVCCPA — that is backwards, corrected against practitioner analysis confirming a creditor collecting its own debt including a bank is fully subject. LOWEST-CONFIDENCE SOL of the batch: § 55-2-6 was NOT fetched verbatim, published summaries disagree on whether card debt is 5 or 10, and 5 rests on the reasoning that an unsigned agreement is not a signed writing. VERIFY § 55-2-6 directly before relying on either number.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.fdcpa_equivalent: Wyoming Collection Agency Act, Wyo. Stat. § 33-11-101 et seq.
WY.fdcpa_note: NO PRIVATE RIGHT OF ACTION and does NOT reach original creditors — licensing and bonding only, exempts persons collecting their own accounts. WCPA § 40-12-108 has a private action but targets deceptive trade practices in consumer sales rather than collection conduct and requires a pre-suit demand. Consumers effectively rely on the federal FDCPA.
WY.garnishment_exempt: 75% exempt; lesser of 25% or excess over 30x federal minimum wage (§ 1-15-511; parallel limit § 40-14-505)
WY.confidence: Fetched verbatim: (a)(i) ten years 'upon a specialty or any contract, agreement or promise in writing'; (a)(ii)(A) eight years 'upon a contract not in writing, either express or implied'. Longest written-contract SOL researched. Card reported as 8 because an issuer-drafted unsigned agreement is most naturally 'not in writing'; counter is 10 under (a)(i). NOTE this is the one state where the card figure is SHORTER than the written figure on a contested basis — confirm before asserting a time-bar.
